question: For a full-rank end-to-end matrix represented by a fixed-depth, fixed-width deep linear network, are balanced factorizations exactly the minimum-regularizer representatives of its parameter fiber, and can fiberwise gradient flows reach balancedness with rigorous convergence guarantees that support a decomposition of training into regularization and learning?

key_findings.claim: Author geometric setup: for square d-by-d factors with full-rank product X, the complete fiber of equivalent network parameters is a GL(d)^(N-1) orbit, while its balanced subset is a compact unitary orbit.
key_findings.evidence: The fiber F_X contains all tuples W=(W_N,...,W_1) with product X. Full rank of X forces every factor to be invertible. Lemma 1 writes every tuple as A acting on an SVD-derived center C, and the equations W_k W_k^*=W_{k+1}^* W_{k+1} define the balanced manifold. The balanced points in the fiber form the U(d)^(N-1) orbit O_X.

key_findings.claim: Author main theorem: on a full-rank fiber, the minimizers of the sum of squared Frobenius norms are exactly the balanced factorizations.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 states argmin_{W in F_X} ||W||_2 equals F_X intersect M. Section 3 identifies the DLN moment map with the imbalance matrices G_k and applies Kempf-Ness to the closed GL orbit; all critical points of the invariant squared norm are global minima and form one unitary orbit. The real case is transferred through Slodowy's real-group extension.

anchors.section: 3.2-3.3, Kempf-Ness Theorems 13-14 and proof of Theorem 1
Completion of Theorem 1 for real matrices and Remark 18

key_findings.claim: Author extension and negative boundary: the same balanced minimizer set holds for summed Schatten p norms when 1<p<infinity, but the practically important p=1 case remains unresolved.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 20 invokes the Azad-Loeb extension for strictly plurisubharmonic functions to obtain argmin_{F_X} ||W||_p=F_X intersect M for 1<p<infinity. The text explicitly says the Schatten-1 norm is not strictly plurisubharmonic, so its critical or minimizing set need not be a single unitary orbit and related flows are left open.

anchors.section: 1.5, regularizing flows and exclusion of p=1

key_findings.claim: Author flow result: the induced-metric gradient flow of the L2 regularizer constrained to a full-rank fiber makes every imbalance moment decay exactly as G_k(t)=G_k(0)e^{-2t}.
key_findings.evidence: The fiber tangent vectors are parameterized by infinitesimal group actions. Lemmas 2-5 express the differential and induced metric through a block-tridiagonal operator H, with grad (1/2)||W||^2=w_b where H_k(b)=G_k. Pushing the negative gradient flow through the moment map gives dot G=-2G, hence exact exponential decay. The rate is exact for moment imbalance; a uniform rate for Euclidean parameter distance to the balanced orbit is not separately established.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the exact v2 PDF contains sign and non-degeneracy errors in the page-12 proof even though the intended corrected calculation supports Theorem 2.
key_findings.evidence: Equation (2.22) is typeset as an equality of two real traces followed by '=0' rather than the needed real trace of their difference, and the next sentence appeals to 'degeneracy' of the inner product although uniqueness requires non-degeneracy. More seriously, equation (2.23) writes dot G=dG w_b=-2G even though dot W=-w_b, so it needs dot G=-dG w_b. Remark 9 then states dG w_b=dG W=-2G, whereas G is quadratic in W and dG_W[W]=+2G. Inserting the missing negative signs yields the announced dot G=-2G; as printed, the proof is internally inconsistent.

key_findings.claim: Author second flow result: squared moment-map descent becomes an explicit cubic balancing system and converges globally to one point of the balanced variety.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 10 computes grad (1/2)||G||^2 as w_{2G}; the negative gradient flow is dot W_k=2(W_k G_{k-1}-G_k W_k). Its moment evolution remains coupled, but the cited general Kirwan-Ness theory yields Corollary 1: every initial W in the full parameter space has a singleton omega-limit on the balanced variety. Unlike the L2 fiber flow, this cubic flow is explicit and does not require solving H(b)=G at every step.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: 'regularization implies balancedness' is a fiberwise representation theorem, not a theorem that ordinary regularized training stays balanced or separates into two timescales.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 1 fixes X exactly and minimizes only over its equivalent factorizations; the regularizing flow is a projected Riemannian gradient tangent to F_X. Ordinary weight decay in equation (4.1) also changes X and couples to the learning gradient. Section 4 explicitly calls fast regularization followed by slow learning an idealization and leaves a Fenichel singular-perturbation justification as future work. The exponential factor becomes 2kappa, which is not automatically fast when regularization strength kappa is small.

anchors.section: 4 and 4.1, idealized two-stage paradigm and equation (4.1)

key_findings.claim: Author geometric synthesis: on the balanced manifold, learning descends the loss while preserving balancedness and projects to a Riemannian gradient flow for the end-to-end matrix.
key_findings.evidence: The imbalance matrices are conserved under gradient flow for any loss that depends only on X, so the zero-moment manifold is invariant. The paper defines learning as grad E restricted to the balanced manifold and cites prior work identifying its projection with dot X=-grad_{g_N} E on matrix space under Riemannian submersion. This is a continuous-time geometric description, not a new convergence theorem for a specified loss.

key_findings.claim: Author interpretation and reviewer caveat: the framework unifies DLN balancedness with norm-balanced linear-system realizations, but calling the minimizing orbit the 'simplest' model is conceptual rather than a statistical or coding-length result.
key_findings.evidence: Sections 1.2-1.4 compare equivalent matrix factorizations with equivalent state-space realizations under GL actions and use Kempf-Ness as the common minimum principle. The minimum Frobenius norm is exact, but the claims about Occam's razor, model reduction, and optimal descriptions are interpretations; no generalization, compression, identifiability, or downstream control metric is analyzed.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the Bayesian section is a research proposal, and its displayed restricted-Gaussian posterior omits a conditioning/disintegration justification.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.3 conditions an ambient Gaussian prior on the exact end-to-end matrix and writes a density proportional to exp(-beta kappa ||W||^2) against induced Hausdorff volume on F_X. Conditioning on a measure-zero level set generally requires a disintegration or coarea factor involving the Jacobian of the product map; the paper neither derives that factor nor proves the asserted small-noise uniform limit on O_X. The authors label the Bayesian development forthcoming and say it is currently precise only for the DLN.

key_findings.claim: Evaluation audit: the paper supplies complete symbolic derivations and scalar schematics but no numerical, optimization, statistical, or real-network experiment.
key_findings.evidence: Figures 1.1-1.3 are conceptual drawings; Figure 1.1 specializes to d=1,N=2 and illustrates the fiber hyperbola and balanced asymptotes. There are no tables, numerical flow integrations, comparisons with Saul's balancing algorithm, discrete-time tests, timing measurements, or nonlinear-network evaluations. Consequently the exact theorems are evaluated only by proof, and every practical training claim remains untested here.

method.core_idea: View all factorizations with the same end-to-end matrix as a group orbit, identify layer imbalance as the moment map for its unitary symmetry, and apply Kempf-Ness/Azad-Loeb minimum principles plus induced Riemannian fiber geometry to characterize balanced minimizers and balancing flows.
method.mechanism: An SVD-derived center and GL(d)^(N-1) action parameterize the full-rank fiber. The moment matrices G_k=W_k W_k^*-W_{k+1}^* W_{k+1} vanish exactly at balanced points. Kempf-Ness makes the zero-moment unitary orbit the L2 minimum. For dynamics, infinitesimal group actions parameterize tangent vectors, a block-tridiagonal operator H represents the induced metric, and pushing the constrained negative gradient through G yields exact linear decay. Differentiating ||G||^2 instead yields an implementable cubic Kirwan-Ness flow.
assumptions: The main results use N square d-by-d matrices of identical width and an end-to-end matrix X of full rank, so every factor is invertible and F_X is one smooth GL(d)^(N-1) orbit.
Matrices are complex with the real Frobenius inner product for the main derivations; the real case is transferred through Slodowy's extension.
The network is exactly linear and the loss depends only on the matrix product X=W_N...W_1.
The balancing dynamics are continuous-time Riemannian gradient flows under the metric induced from Euclidean parameter space.
The L2 regularizing flow is constrained to a fixed fiber and requires solving the block-tridiagonal linear system H(b)=G at each state.
The Schatten-p extension assumes 1<p<infinity and strict plurisubharmonicity; p=1 is excluded.
The fast-slow, noisy, Bayesian, and model-reduction interpretations are proposals beyond the proved minimum and flow theorems.

techniques.role: Represents every full-rank equivalent factorization by a GL(d)^(N-1) action on an SVD center.
Encodes adjacent-layer Gram mismatch as Hermitian moment matrices whose zero set is balanced.
Turns the closed group orbit and unitary-invariant norm into a global balanced-minimizer characterization.
Projects regularizer descent onto a fixed product fiber using tangent group directions and the induced Euclidean metric.
Solves H(b)=G to express the L2 fiber gradient and expose exact moment decay.
Differentiates squared moment imbalance to obtain an explicit globally convergent balancing ODE.
Relates balanced parameter-space descent to end-to-end matrix descent under an induced metric.

evaluations.setting: Full-rank X in complex or real d-by-d matrices, depth N, with all exact factorizations constrained to F_X.
evaluations.metric: Sum of squared Frobenius norms over layers.
evaluations.result: Theorem 1 identifies the complete argmin as the balanced unitary orbit F_X intersect M.
evaluations.baseline: All unbalanced GL(d)^(N-1)-equivalent factorizations of the same X.

evaluations.setting: Continuous induced-metric negative gradient flow of (1/2)||W||^2 on a full-rank fiber.
evaluations.result: After correcting the printed sign omissions in the proof, G_k(t)=G_k(0)e^{-2t} exactly for all k; no parameter-distance rate or numerical integration is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Initial fixed-product factorization with moment G(0); no competing balancing algorithm is evaluated.

evaluations.setting: Squared-moment descent on the full deep-linear parameter space.
evaluations.metric: Asymptotic omega-limit and squared moment norm.
evaluations.result: The cubic ODE is explicit, monotonically decreases squared imbalance, and is asserted via general theory to converge from every initialization to one balanced point; no finite-time rate is given.
evaluations.baseline: The implicit L2 fiber flow, which has exact moment rate but requires a linear solve at every state.

evaluations.setting: Full-rank fiber with summed Schatten p norms for 1<p<infinity.
evaluations.result: Theorem 20 gives the same balanced orbit as the complete minimum set; p=1 is explicitly unresolved.
evaluations.baseline: The L2 special case of Theorem 1.

evaluations.setting: Scalar schematic d=1,N=2 and conceptual higher-dimensional flow diagrams.
evaluations.metric: Visual intersection of a product fiber with balanced loci.
evaluations.result: The hyperbola w_2 w_1=x is minimized at its balanced intersections and the drawings depict regularizing versus learning directions.
evaluations.baseline: No empirical, numerical, discrete-time, nonlinear-network, or runtime baseline is provided.

limitations: Author-stated: the main exposition assumes full-rank X; lower-rank strata require additional geometric care even though some calculations may extend.
Author-stated: Schatten p=1 regularization is not covered because strict plurisubharmonicity fails, and its critical set and flow remain open.
Author-stated: the fast-regularization/slow-learning decomposition, stochastic Riemannian dynamics, and Bayesian development are future work.

Reviewer-identified: all proved network results are for square, constant-width, deep linear networks in continuous time, not rectangular layers, nonlinearities, biases, SGD, momentum, Adam, or finite-step weight decay.
Reviewer-identified: the exact v2 proof of Theorem 2 contains malformed trace, non-degeneracy, and sign statements that must be repaired before formal reuse.
Reviewer-identified: exponential convergence is exact in moment-map coordinates; the paper does not state or prove the same uniform constant for Euclidean distance in W to the balanced orbit.
Reviewer-identified: the L2 fiber gradient is implicit and may be costly or ill-conditioned because H(b)=G must be solved at every step.
Reviewer-identified: there is no numerical or empirical validation, no discrete implementation, and no comparison to existing balancing fixes or flows.
Reviewer-identified: ordinary regularized training changes X, so the fixed-fiber theorem alone does not establish balancedness of a regularized optimizer's entire trajectory or solution.
Reviewer-identified: the displayed conditional Gaussian measure on an exact product fiber is not derived by disintegration or coarea and may omit a Jacobian density factor.
failure_modes: If X is rank deficient, the fiber can be singular and can contain factors of different ranks, so the single smooth group-orbit and tangent-space calculations used by the main proofs fail.
Rectangular or varying-width factors are outside the stated group action and may have additional gauge directions and strata.
A finite-step optimizer does not preserve the continuous-flow moment laws exactly, and stochastic gradients, momentum, or adaptive preconditioning can break the invariant geometry.
Unconstrained L2 weight decay moves normal to the fixed-product fiber as well as along it, so the isolated regularizing flow is not the actual weight-decay update.
Small kappa makes the proposed regularization rate 2kappa slow rather than fast, undermining timescale separation unless learning is slower still and a singular-perturbation condition is proved.
Moment imbalance can decay quickly without an established uniform conversion to parameter distance or numerical conditioning near the balanced orbit.
Solving H(b)=G can become numerically unstable near rank loss, while the explicit cubic flow has no closed moment-rate guarantee.
The naive Hausdorff-restricted posterior can differ from the regular conditional law if the product-map Jacobian varies over the fiber.
reusable_insights: Analyze overparameterized models by separating observable coordinates from fibers of functionally equivalent parameters.
A symmetry's moment map can turn a qualitative balance condition into an algebraic residual with a tractable flow.
Minimizing a regularizer within an equivalence class is distinct from minimizing a regularized prediction loss; keep these optimization problems separate.
An implicit gradient flow may have a simple closed evolution after pushing it through the right invariant statistic.
Use compact-group orbits to identify all equivalent minimizers rather than choosing one arbitrary gauge-fixed representative.
When proposing conditional Bayesian measures on level sets, derive the reference density through coarea or disintegration before applying Laplace asymptotics.
Report convergence coordinates explicitly: exponential decay of a residual does not automatically equal exponential distance-to-set convergence.
open_questions: Can Theorem 2 be restated and proved without the page-12 sign and non-degeneracy errors, including a quantitative parameter-distance rate?
What are the complete minimum sets and balancing flows for Schatten-1 or entrywise L1 regularization?
How do the minimum principle and flows extend to rank-deficient X, rectangular layers, unequal widths, and the singular rank stratification?
Can a stable, efficient discretization of the implicit H(b)=G flow or the explicit cubic flow outperform Saul's balancing fix in computation and conditioning?

Under what scaling of kappa, learning rate, curvature, and noise can geometric singular perturbation rigorously reduce ordinary regularized training to fast fiber relaxation plus slow balanced learning?
Which parts of the moment-map framework survive homogeneous nonlinearities, residual connections, convolutional sharing, and transformers?
What is the correct regular conditional Gaussian density on a product fiber, and does its small-noise limit have exactly uniform mass along the balanced orbit?
Do balanced representatives improve any empirical generalization, robustness, compression, or optimization metric beyond minimizing parameter norm at fixed X?

competitive_landscape.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational direct predecessor on balancedness and conservation under gradient flow.
competitive_landscape.difference: Du, Hu, and Lee prove invariance of adjacent layer squared-norm differences for deep homogeneous models and finite-step results for matrix factorization; this paper strengthens balance for full-rank DLNs to aligned Gram matrices, derives a fiberwise minimum principle, and constructs separate balancing flows through GIT.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2018 proceedings version, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 31

competitive_landscape.title: On the Optimization of Deep Networks: Implicit Acceleration by Overparameterization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational deep-linear optimization and balancedness predecessor.
competitive_landscape.difference: Arora, Cohen, and Hazan study how depth changes end-to-end gradient dynamics and can accelerate optimization; this paper focuses on the geometry of equivalent factorizations, regularizer minima, and moment-map balancing rather than convergence of a specified prediction loss.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 80, ICML 2018 published proceedings version

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Descent Aligns the Layers of Deep Linear Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct predecessor on layer alignment under learning dynamics.
competitive_landscape.difference: Ji and Telgarsky prove asymptotic rank-one alignment and max-margin direction for gradient descent/flow on separable data; this paper instead characterizes full-rank balanced Gram alignment at fixed X and introduces independent regularizing flows, without a supervised-loss convergence theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Weight-Balancing Fixes and Flows for Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest prior minimum-balancing algorithm and flow.
competitive_landscape.difference: Saul gives convergent multiplicative gauge-fixing algorithms and balancing flows for homogeneous nonlinear networks and l_{p,q} regularizers; this paper uses full matrix GL symmetry and Kempf-Ness on square DLN fibers, obtaining Gram-level balance and an exact moment-decay flow but no discrete algorithm evaluation.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Transactions on Machine Learning Research published version, September 2023

competitive_landscape.title: The Geometry of the Set of Equivalent Linear Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Shewchuk and Bhattacharya characterize rank strata, tangent and normal spaces, dimensions, and topology for general equivalent linear networks; this paper restricts its main calculations to the smooth full-rank square stratum and adds invariant-norm minimum and balancing-flow results.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:2404.14855v1, submitted 23 April 2024 and still current

competitive_landscape.title: Geometry of fibers of the multiplication map of deep linear neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Pepin Lehalleur and Rimanyi use quiver representations to determine codimension, irreducible components, permutation invariance, and singular-learning quantities for multiplication fibers; this paper uses the full-rank orbit where singularities disappear and studies balanced variational and dynamic structure.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:2411.19920v2, revised 11 December 2024 and still current

competitive_landscape.title: An entropy formula for the Deep Linear Network
competitive_landscape.relationship: Immediate same-program predecessor on balanced-manifold geometry and Riemannian submersion.
competitive_landscape.difference: Menon and Yu develop the balanced manifold, group-orbit foliation, induced observable-space metric, and entropy formula; this paper reuses that geometry to add Kempf-Ness regularizer minima and two fiber-balancing flows.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv:2509.09088v3, SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis accepted final version revised 20 May 2026

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a new GIT foundation for DLN balancedness: L2 and Schatten-p regularization select precisely the balanced orbit, the induced-fiber L2 flow has uniform exponential moment decay, the squared-moment flow is an explicit globally convergent cubic system, and these structures support a fast-slow, model-reduction, and Bayesian paradigm for learning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Theorem 1 applies Kempf-Ness to the full-rank DLN fiber; Theorem 2 derives G(t)=G(0)e^{-2t}; Theorem 10 computes the cubic Kirwan-Ness flow and cites global convergence; Theorem 20 invokes Azad-Loeb for 1<p<infinity. Sections 4.1-4.3 explicitly label the fast-slow and Bayesian developments heuristic or forthcoming.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the combination of full matrix gauge symmetry, Kempf-Ness/Azad-Loeb minimum principles, and induced-fiber dynamics yielding a closed exponential law for Gram imbalance plus an explicit cubic alternative. Balancedness conservation, layer alignment, minimum-norm gauge fixing, balancing algorithms, and detailed fiber geometry all predate the paper, including a close 2023 TMLR flow treatment and the authors' own immediate geometric precursor. The minimum and flow theorems are mathematically substantive within the full-rank square DLN, but the practical training, Occam, fast-slow, and Bayesian conclusions remain interpretations; page-12 sign and non-degeneracy errors also require correction. Overall novelty is high for the particular GIT/Riemannian synthesis, moderate relative to prior balancing work, and unestablished for real deep-learning practice.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text pass over every page of the 20-page pinned PDF, including all displayed proofs, three schematic figures, discussion, limitations, and complete references; there are no appendices or tables. The official arXiv record checked 2026-08-23 identifies the current source as arXiv:2511.01137v2 (23 March 2026), consistent with the extraction made that day, while the immutable review pin is the indexed PDF/text hash above. The page-12 typesetting/sign audit was checked against a high-resolution rendering of the exact pinned PDF, not inferred from extraction noise. Seven direct current primary records were checked at official proceedings, OpenReview, and exact arXiv revisions. Confidence is high in coverage and scope comparisons, but formal verification should include an independent geometer correcting Lemma 5/Theorem 2's printed proof and checking the claimed global Kirwan-Ness corollary.
